articles.title: MAGA pollster warns Republicans sleeping as red states slip from their grasp
articles.description: A MAGA pollster who called President Donald Trump's last two White House wins warned Republicans are sleeping on red states now slipping toward Democrats. In a Wednesday episode of Bulwark Takes , Rich Baris laid out the case during an interview with former GOP operative Tim Miller . Baris, the director of Big Data Poll, argued that the party is coasting on Trump's 2024 margins in states he won't be on the ballot to defend. "Republicans are going to run out of a coalition soon if they don't build on what he started to build in '24," Baris said. He pointed to a cluster of seats that the GOP treats as locked down. The Republicans' assumption is "hubris," Baris said. "They just thought Ohio and Iowa and even Texas would be within their grasp forever because of how Donald Trump performed in them," Baris said. "It's hubris. I don't know what else to call it." Republicans have "repeatedly understated Democrats' chances" in Kansas, Nebraska, and Montana, Baris said. He described those three states as a "sleeper" cluster with "longtime populist and progressive roots that aren't as red as people seem to think." Baris was blunter still about Texas, where the party redrew congressional maps off Trump's numbers. "You don't perform like Donald Trump performs in Texas, folks. I hate to tell you, you don't," Baris said. "Hispanics don't like you the way that they like Trump in 2024." He said the party built those maps "with the same arrogance," using Trump's ceiling as a floor and treating gains he called "squandered" as permanent. Cost of living will be the biggest issue for voters, Baris warned. "Socialism" attacks fall flat with voters when "you can't pay your own bills," Baris said. "They're much more afraid that they can't pay their rent or their car payment or get back-to-school clothes for their kids and fill up the refrigerator than they are about Republicans throwing around the word 'socialism,'" Baris said.

articles.title: AJK PM orders bureaucracy to gear up for 100-day reform agenda
articles.description: MUZAFFARABAD: Azad Jam­mu and Kashmir (AJK) Prime Min­ister Iftikhar Gillani on Wednesday directed the bureaucracy to gear up for implementation of the government’s 100-day reform agenda , saying his foremost priority was to introduce systemic reforms to ease the difficulties of the common man and create new opportunities. Speaking at his first meeting with government secretaries at the Prime Minister’s Secretariat, Mr Gillani said his government had come to serve the people and its performance would be visible “on the ground”. “Our foremost priority is to bring reforms to the system, create ease for the common man and generate new opportunities,” he said, adding that the government would address the challenges facing the state with the cooperation of the bureaucracy. He said the administrative mach­inery had important responsibilities in translating government policies into tangible results and stres­sed the need for collective efforts. “The success of any government largely depends on the efficiency, commitment and sense of responsibility of its administrative machinery. I expect the AJK bureaucracy to work with dedication and a sense of urgency to implement the reform agenda in letter and spirit,” he said. Mr Gillani said the government would provide all necessary support to officials to deliver meaningful reforms and improve public service delivery. He said unemployment was a major challenge in the state and announced plans to introduce a youth engagement programme and demand-based skills development programmes in the social sector. He also promised relief to people in transport and healthcare services, saying measures would be taken on a priority basis to reduce their difficulties. ‘Practical measures’ The prime minister said the government was committed to translating its reform programme into practical measures and making its impact visible to the people. He said the 100-day agenda also demonstrated the seriousness of the party’s central leadership towards AJK. Separately, the prime minister attended briefings by Chief Secretary Khushal Khan and Inspector Gen­eral of Police (IGP) retired Capt Lia­qat Ali Malik on the organisational structures of the Services and General Administration Depart­ment and the police department, respectively. The IGP also briefed the prime minister on the department’s performance and future needs, as well as the overall law and order situation in the territory. Earlier, upon his arrival at the Prime Minister’s Secretariat, Mr Gillani was received by his principal secretary and officers and staff of the secretariat. Published in Dawn, September 3rd, 2026

articles.title: Max Miller dodges Trump party for 'time with family' amid abuse allegations
articles.description: Rep. Max Miller (R-OH), accused of abusing his ex-wife and toddler daughter, turned down an invitation to President Donald Trump's first-ever midterm convention to spend time with his family. Miller is one of several endangered Republicans staying home rather than joining the president in Dallas, the New York Times reported Tuesday. The Dallas gathering on Sept. 9 and 10 is the first midterm convention either major party has held, and Trump is scheduled to headline both nights. Lawmakers are being charged $25,000 to attend, according to the Times. "I was invited, but staying home to campaign and spend time with family," Miller told the newspaper. The Times described Miller as an embattled Republican fighting to keep his seat after allegations of domestic abuse upended his campaign. The family Miller says he is staying home with is the same family at the center of those allegations, which involve his ex-wife and their 2-year-old daughter. Emily Moreno told police she noticed a large bruise on the couple's daughter during a bath in February 2025, CNN reported . Miller asked to see a photograph of the injury, which turned out to be a broken collarbone, and the discovery prompted a police investigation. The child had a right clavicle fracture and "a bruise that accompanies the injury that appears to be in a handprint and appears to have been inflicted," according to the child protection team's findings in the police report. CNN's Jake Tapper pressed him on that finding during an August interview, along with what the child reportedly said in the days before the injury was found. "Daddy angry" and "daddy's house is scary," the child told her mother, Emily Moreno, police said, along with the phrase "daddy kill you." Miller answered that his daughter was 2 years old and could not "string sentences together like that," Tapper's interview showed. The congressman had said moments earlier that the child made similar remarks about her mother, and when Tapper noted the contradiction, Miller pivoted to a complaint about due process. Emily Moreno is the daughter of Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-OH), and her allegations against Miller extend well beyond the collarbone injury. Miller "previously held a gun to her head as well," a police officer wrote after taking her statement on Feb. 1, CBS News reported . That detail did not appear in the copy of the police report Miller later posted online, NBC affiliate WCMH found when it compared his files against court records. Emily Moreno said she told Miller in June 2024 that she planned to leave him, according to CBS News. Miller then allegedly "threw onto Ms. Moreno hot water from a pan of eggs he'd just cooked." She photographed red marks on her chest and says he also sprayed her with the kitchen sink nozzle, WCMH reported. Miller has called the sprayer incident "horseplay" and said the water was not scalding. Court records show Emily Moreno also accused Miller of attacking her in February of this year, after their divorce. Emily Moreno said her ex-husband "trashed me and pushed me and threw me to the ground" in the filings. Miller has argued that she attended a child's birthday party after the alleged assault, which he says shows no abuse occurred. Emily Moreno strongly disagrees. In another lawsuit, Emily Moreno alleged that Miller and his attorney Aaron Minc "recklessly published and disclosed to the world a nude image" of the couple's daughter. The link stayed up for 23 hours, drew more than 400,000 views, and she is seeking $150,000 in damages each time the image is downloaded. Miller's lawyer later took responsibility for the published image. In a recent interview, Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-OH) told reporters that Miller had refused to return his granddaughter's blue stuffed bunny over the weekend. "This girl is crying at night because she can't sleep without her little blue bunny. His answer is 'I'm just not gonna give it to you,'" Sen. Bernie Moreno said, calling it a level of total and complete depravity. Leaked text messages published by the New Republic show that the dispute began months earlier, and that an attorney for Emily Moreno emailed Miller's lawyers on Aug. 3, asking them to "have Max return the bunny forthwith." The police investigation into the collarbone injury ended without charges, and Miller retains joint custody of his daughter. He denies every allegation and has accused Emily Moreno of abusing the child herself. Miller asked the House Ethics Committee to investigate him in an effort to clear his name, and the panel announced in August that it had opened an inquiry into the abuse and drug-use claims. "I have absolutely nothing to hide," he said. The embattled lawmaker's decision to skip the event comes after Trump has defended him at nearly every stage, beginning with the 2021 endorsement that launched his congressional career. Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office last month, Trump called the allegations against Miller "a very sad thing." "I know Max. He's a good person," Trump insisted at the time, adding that he would "let the families figure that out." Trump's team then asked Ohio Republicans to stop pressuring Miller to quit the race, reversing an effort that other Republicans and some White House officials had already started, Politico reported . "They basically told us to back off," one Ohio Republican told Politico, "and let the voters decide." Sen. Jon Husted (R-OH), who has called on Miller to resign, is not staying home. Husted is billed as a speaker in Dallas, according to plans shared with the Times.

articles.title: The deportation of Milo Yiannopoulos signals a rupture within Maga | Moira Donegan
articles.description: The far-right provocateur helped galvanize a movement that no longer needs him. Now his imitators are claiming victory It’s been a long, slow decline for Milo Yiannopoulos. From the vantage point of 2026, it’s easy to forget that he was once a big deal. The British-born far-right provocateur, who was arrested by ICE in Louisiana and deported from the US this week, was among the first media figures to ride the “ gamergate ” controversy and ensuing rightwing populist wave that brought Donald Trump to office in 2016. An editor of the then ascendant Breitbart News from 2014 to 2017, Yiannopoulous was an early adopter of the media strategy of algorithm-optimized outrage bait, trawling the internet and a consulting large network of well-placed sources in search of stories he could use to fan the flames of online culture war discourses. He would write a story mocking a feminist, or fire off a tweet saying something racist about Muslims, and the ensuing firestorm of controversy would result in online arguments, media coverage, and his own promptly and decisively rising star. Rinse, repeat. Continue reading...
